summary.title: MAXIMAL ABELIAN EXTENSION OF A MODULAR CURVE UNRAMIFIED OUTSIDE CUSPS
summary.executive_summary: This paper investigates the geometrically maximal abelian coverings of the modular curve $X_0(p)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, specifically focusing on the open subscheme $Y_0(p)$ obtained by removing the cusps. While Mazur previously established that the Shimura covering $X_2(p) \to X_0(p)$ is the geometrically maximal unramified abelian covering of the full curve $X_0(p)$, the authors address the distinct case where ramification is allowed at the cusps. They prove that there exists a cyclic covering $X'_2(p) \to X_0(p)$ of degree $2N_p$, where $N_p = (p-1)/\gcd(p-1, 12)$, which is geometrically maximal for $Y_0(p)$. This new covering $X'_2(p)$ factors through the Shimura curve $X_2(p)$ via a degree-two covering $\pi_p$ that is unramified outside the cusps. The construction relies on the theory of generalized Dedekind eta functions (Siegel functions) to explicitly define the function field of $X'_2(p)$ as a quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}(X_2(p))$. The authors demonstrate that the square of a specific modular function $F_h$, constructed from products of eta functions, generates this extension. They verify that this function has odd order at the cusps and is constant elsewhere, ensuring the required ramification profile. The result extends the understanding of the abelian fundamental group of modular curves by incorporating the generalized Jacobian with modulus at the cusps. The paper provides a complete classification of this maximal extension for all primes $p$, handling the special case $p \equiv 11 \pmod{12}$ separately due to the structure of the relevant congruence subgroups. This work bridges the gap between the unramified theory of Mazur and the more general theory of abelian coverings with controlled ramification, offering explicit tools for studying the arithmetic of these curves.

claims.description: The geometrically maximal abelian covering of $Y_0(p)$ is cyclic of degree $2N_p$.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper investigates the geometrically maximal abelian coverings of the modular curve $X_0(p)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, specifically focusing on the open subscheme $Y_0(p)$ obtained by removing the cusps. While Mazur previously established that the Shimura covering $X_2(p) \to X_0(p)$ is the geometrically maximal unramified abelian covering of the full curve $X_0(p)$, the authors address the distinct case where ramification is allowed at the cusps. They prove that there exists a cyclic covering $X'_2(p) \to X_0(p)$ of degree $2N_p$, where $N_p = (p-1)/\gcd(p-1, 12)$, which is geometrically maximal for $Y_0(p)$. This new covering $X'_2(p)$ factors through the Shimura curve $X_2(p)$ via a degree-two covering $\pi_p$ that is unramified outside the cusps. The construction relies on the theory of generalized Dedekind eta functions (Siegel functions) to explicitly define the function field of $X'_2(p)$ as a quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}(X_2(p))$. The authors demonstrate that the square of a specific modular function $F_h$, constructed from products of eta functions, generates this extension. They verify that this function has odd order at the cusps and is constant elsewhere, ensuring the required ramification profile. The result extends the understanding of the abelian fundamental group of modular curves by incorporating the generalized Jacobian with modulus at the cusps. The paper provides a complete classification of this maximal extension for all primes $p$, handling the special case $p \equiv 11 \pmod{12}$ separately due to the structure of the relevant congruence subgroups. This work bridges the gap between the unramified theory of Mazur and the more general theory of abelian coverings with controlled ramification, offering explicit tools for studying the arithmetic of these curves.

Research Context
Mazur proved that the Shimura covering is the geometrically maximal unramified abelian covering of $X_0(p)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. This covering is a unique subcovering of $X_1(p) \to X_0(p)$ of degree $N_p$. The degree is defined as $N_p := (p - 1)/ \gcd(p - 1, 12)$. The current study focuses on coverings unramified outside the cusps of $X_0(p)$. This allows for a larger abelian extension compared to the strictly unramified case. The goal is to construct a geometrically maximal abelian covering of the open curve $Y_0(p)$.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is to identify the geometrically maximal abelian covering of $Y_0(p)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. The authors hypothesize that this covering is cyclic of degree $2N_p$. They propose that this covering factors through the Shimura curve $X_2(p)$. The intermediate step is a degree two covering $\pi_p: X'_2(p) \to X_2(p)$. This degree two covering is unramified outside the cusps. The function field of $X'_2(p)$ is a quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}(X_2(p))$. This extension is generated by the square root of a rational function.

Methodological Details
The study considers modular curves $X_0(p)$ and $X_1(p)$ as smooth proper curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The open subscheme $Y_0(p)$ is defined by removing the two cusps from $X_0(p)$. The generalized Jacobian $\hat{J} = \text{Jac}(X, D)$ is used with modulus $D$ at the cusps. The group $M_{\text{Tor}}$ is defined as $\text{Hom}(T\hat{J}, \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}(1))$. The geometrically maximal covering corresponds to the dual of the $\mu$-type subgroup $M^\mu_{\text{Tor}}(-1)$. For $p \ge 5$, the construction uses generalized Dedekind eta functions $E_g$. The function $F_h$ is defined as a product of eta functions raised to a power. The case $p \equiv 11 \pmod{12}$ requires a different construction using triplets of integers.

Procedures And Architectures
The authors define the group $\Gamma'_2(p)$ as the kernel of a specific character on $\Gamma_2(p)$. This character involves the sign character $\psi$ and potentially another character $\chi$. The modular curve $X'_2(p)$ is associated with the subgroup $\Gamma'_2(p)$. The function $F_h$ is shown to transform under $\Gamma_0(p)$ by the character $\psi$. The square $F_h^2$ is a modular function on $X_2(p)$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$. The order of $F_h^2$ at any cusp of $X_2(p)$ is proven to be odd. The order of $F_h^2$ is zero at all non-cusp points. This ramification profile ensures the covering is unramified outside the cusps.

Key Results
There exists a cyclic covering $f'_p: X'_2(p) \to X_0(p)$ of degree $2N_p$. This covering is geometrically maximal for the open curve $Y_0(p)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. The covering factors as $f'_p = f_p \circ \pi_p$, where $\pi_p$ has degree two. The covering $\pi_p: X'_2(p) \to X_2(p)$ is unramified outside the cusps. The function field $\mathbb{Q}(X'_2(p))$ is a quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}(X_2(p))$. This extension is generated by the square root of $F_h^2$. The result holds for all primes $p$, including the special case $p \equiv 11 \pmod{12}$.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The result extends Mazur's theorem on unramified coverings to the case with cusp ramification. It identifies the precise structure of the maximal abelian extension of the open modular curve. The use of generalized eta functions provides an explicit arithmetic description of the covering. The cyclic nature of the covering simplifies the Galois group structure to $\mathbb{Z}/2N_p\mathbb{Z}$. This connects the geometry of modular curves to the arithmetic of their function fields.

Contradictions And Limitations
The construction for $p \equiv 11 \pmod{12}$ requires a separate treatment due to group structure. The paper assumes $p$ is a prime number for the main results. The case $p=2$ or $p=3$ is handled trivially via $\mathbb{G}_m$ identification. The proof relies on the finiteness of the geometric fundamental group.

Claims
The geometrically maximal abelian covering of $Y_0(p)$ is cyclic of degree $2N_p$. The covering $f'_p$ is cyclic of degree $2N_p$. It is geometrically maximal for $Y_0(p)$. Mazur's result applies to the unramified case, not this one. This defines the full abelian fundamental group of the open curve.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The authors verify the ramification order of $F_h^2$ at all cusps. They handle the case $p \equiv 11 \pmod{12}$ with a different function $G_h$. The transformation properties of $F_h$ under $\Gamma_0(p)$ are explicitly calculated.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 illustrates the commutative diagram of the coverings $X'_2(p)$, $X_2(p)$, and $X_0(p)$. The diagram shows $\pi_p$ as a degree two covering.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the identification of the maximal abelian covering of $Y_0(p)$ as a cyclic degree $2N_p$ cover. 2. The strongest evidence is the explicit construction using generalized Dedekind eta functions with verified ramification. 3. The future path involves applying this explicit model to further arithmetic questions on modular curves.
